   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   176	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   179	open.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they
   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   187	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   188	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   189	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   190	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   191	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   192	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   193	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   194	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   195	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   196	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   197	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   198	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   199	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   200	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   201	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   202	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   203	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   204	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   205	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   206	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   207	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   208	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   209	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   210	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   211	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   212	
   213	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   214	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   215	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   216	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   217	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   218	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   219	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   220	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   221	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   222	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   223	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   224	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   225	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   226	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   227	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   228	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   229	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   230	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   231	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's
   232	carry only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   233	$\chi^{-1}(i)$, and removing this dependence runs into the fiber-averaging
   234	difficulty made explicit under the candidate repairs: averaging preserves
   235	the line-versus-point branches exactly but not the synchronicity branches.
   236	(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
   237	in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
   238	matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
   239	rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
   240	rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
   241	the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
   242	(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
   243	questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
   244	$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
   245	which the test has no counterpart branch.
   246	Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
   247	measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
   248	first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
   249	measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
   250	in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
   251	of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
   252	difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
   253	they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
   254	own value bound.
   255	
   256	\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}
   257	Theorem~4.7 requires $K \ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source
   258	instantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff
   259	$(m')^2 d \ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \ge 1$ when $m' \ge 5$,
   260	holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when
   261	$m' \le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the
   262	admissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's
   263	instantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \in \{1,2\}$ for
   264	every $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ --- in particular, in the
   265	multilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \le 4$.  A candidate
   266	repair is to instantiate $K = \max((m')^3 d,\, 12 m'(d+1))$; the open
   267	obligation is then to re-absorb the error, that is, to check that
   268	$\mathrm{poly}(m',t,K)$ and $e^{-K/(m')^2}$ still collapse to the form
   269	$a(dm')^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bm'd})$ in the small-$m'$ cases where the
   270	maximum is $12m'(d+1)$ --- plausible, since there
   271	$e^{-K/(m')^2} = e^{-12(d+1)/m'}$ decays in $d$ at a rate comparable to
   272	$2^{-m'd}$ for $m' \le 4$, but not checked here.
   273	
   274	In the correspondence of Obligation~1, the only role of the divisibility
   275	$m' \mid q$ is to make the $\chi$-sampled index uniform.  The underlying
   276	mathematics does not need the divisibility.  The low
   277	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} samples its axis
   278	index $i$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly, with no index function
   279	on $\F_q$ and no divisibility hypothesis,%
   280	\footnote{See the test figure in \path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}.}
   281	and the tensor-code test is likewise a test about the code
   282	$\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$, not about an encoding of indices into $\F_q$.  The
   283	$\chi$-based packaging exists so that the question distribution is
   284	conditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the
   285	game the players actually play --- the Pauli basis test at dimension $m$,
   286	where admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension
   287	$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the
   288	proof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question
   289	distribution to be conditionally linear.

   292	
   293	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
   294	Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
   295	$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
   296	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   297	$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
   298	this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,
   299	for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed
   300	$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game
   301	(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing
   302	else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
   303	lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
   304	does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
   305	the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
   306	arbitrary dimension.
   307	
   308	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
   337	  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
   339	  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
   340	  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
   341	  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
   342	  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
   343	  branch value is the diagonal average
   344	  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
   345	  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
   346	  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
   347	  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
   348	  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
   349	  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
   350	  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
   351	  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
   352	  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
   353	  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
   354	  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
   355	  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
   356	  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
   357	  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
   358	  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
   359	  obligation.
   360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
   364	  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
   365	  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
   366	  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
   367	  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
   368	  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
   369	  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
   370	  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
   371	  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
   373	  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
   374	  the import.)
   375	\end{itemize}
   376	
   377	The combining subtree would then be reread with the direct distribution
   378	and the directly indexed game at dimension $2m+2$: every statement becomes
   379	well defined for all admissible tuples, and the expectation is that the
   380	proofs survive unchanged, because the measurements constructed there are
   381	indexed by the geometric data --- points, lines, and polynomials on them
   382	--- and so constitute a strategy for the directly indexed game outright,
   383	with no fiber averaging.  Verifying, lemma by lemma, that those proofs use
   384	only the laws of the sampled objects and never the conditional linearity
   385	of the sampling is part of this direction's obligations.  This follows the
   386	subtree protocol for a definition-level mismatch: the definition is
   387	corrected at the lowest point rather than each downstream lemma acquiring
   388	a hypothesis.  The transport layer costs one parsing-map definition, the
   389	distribution lemma, the pullback lemma, whichever synchronicity control is
   390	chosen, and the dilation--compression lemma; the first three are an
   391	estimated one to two hundred lines on top of the restated import, with the
   392	blueprint's existing Naimark interface supplying the dilation, while the
   393	synchronicity control is the step whose weight is genuinely uncertain.
   394	The external check that the tensor-code test of arXiv:2111.08131 samples
   395	its axes and subcubes directly has been made against that source: Figure~1
   396	there draws the axis index and the subcube data uniformly and directly,
   397	with no index encoding into $\F_q$.
   398	
   399	\paragraph{Padding the dimension.}
   400	Alternatively, embed the combined polynomial into
   401	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,\bar m}(\F_q)$ for $\bar m = 4m$, the least power of two
   402	with $\bar m \ge 2m+2$, ignoring the $2m-2$ dummy variables.  Then
   403	$\bar m \mid q$ holds whenever $q \ge 4m$, and the existing game applies at
   404	dimension $\bar m$.  In the complementary regime $m \in \{q/2,\, q\}$ the
   405	conclusion is vacuous: $md \ge q/2$ gives
   406	$\delta_S \ge a(md)^a q^{-b} \ge a\,2^{-a} q^{a-b} \ge a\,2^{-b} \ge 1$
   407	for $a \ge 2$, while the consistency quantities bounded by the theorem never
   408	exceed $1$.  This route stays inside the present definitions but reworks the
   409	sub-line distribution (a fourth coordinate block of dummies), the combining
   410	map, and the wrong-block Schwartz--Zippel analysis, and it moves the
   411	combining lemmas away from their source statements at dimension $2m+2$.
   412	
   413	\paragraph{Unequal index classes.}
   414	One could instead define an index function at dimension $2m+2$ with classes
   415	of sizes $\lfloor q/(2m+2)\rfloor$ and $\lceil q/(2m+2)\rceil$.  The index
   416	is then only approximately uniform, the identification with the external
   417	test fails exactly, and every distributional identity in the sub-line
   418	analysis acquires an error term; this amounts to re-proving the imported
   419	soundness theorem for a perturbed game and is not recommended.
   420	
   421	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   422	
   423	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} keeps the sub-line lemma, the
   424	combined line lemma, and the polynomial-pair lemma in their source-shaped
   425	statements, with no divisibility hypothesis.  Their proofs retain the source
   426	constructions and mark the unresolved obligation at the exact steps: the
   427	first sampling step of the sub-line construction, where $\chi_{2m+2}$ and
   428	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ are invoked, and the
   429	instantiation step of the polynomial-pair proof, where $(q,2m+2,d,1)$ is
   430	used as a game parameter tuple.  A chapter remark records the divisibility
   431	arithmetic and cites this note; the final soundness theorem for the Pauli
   432	basis test remains open modulo this obligation.  The blueprint's proof node
   433	for the classical soundness import itself states the source's route --- the
   434	identification with the two-prover tensor-code test and the application of
   435	Theorem~4.7 --- and enumerates the two obligations of
   436	Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations} as open, citing this note for the
   437	detailed comparison and the case arithmetic.  An earlier revision had
   438	instead added the hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$ to the three lemmas; that was
   439	statement drift in the sense of the proof-gap protocol, since the hypothesis
   440	excludes all admissible $m \ge 2$ and does not appear in the source.
   441	
   442	\section{Conclusion}
   443	
   444	There is a theorem-level gap in the source proof route: the classical low
   445	individual degree game invoked at dimension $2m+2$ is undefined for every
   446	admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ (and for $(q,m) = (2,1)$), because its
   447	question distribution requires $2m+2 \mid q$ while admissibility supplies
   448	only $m \mid q$.  The cited route therefore does not establish the
   449	polynomial-pair lemma, nor the soundness of the Pauli basis test that
   450	depends on it, beyond $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.  Independently of the
   451	divisibility, the import of the classical game's quantum soundness carries
   452	the two open verification obligations of
   453	Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}: the asserted identity with the
   454	two-prover tensor-code test must be replaced by a reduction carrying a
   455	value bound, and the source's instantiation of the auxiliary parameter
   456	violates the theorem's lower bound at the small dimensions listed there.
   457	We do not assert that any conclusion is false: the underlying tensor-code
   458	soundness is insensitive to how the axis index is sampled, and both import
   459	obligations concern verification, not counterexample.  For the divisibility
   460	repair, the recommended candidate direction is direct index sampling ---
   461	restate the imported soundness theorem for the directly indexed game at
   462	arbitrary dimension; prove the distribution and parsing-pullback lemmas;
   463	settle the synchronicity control for de-seeding together with the
   464	dilation--compression round trip, so that the present soundness statement
   465	would follow from the repaired import; and reread the combining subtree
   466	against the directly indexed game --- a direction whose open obligations
   467	are enumerated under the candidate repairs, not an established route, with
   468	dimension padding as the fallback confined to the present game definition.

1	# Blueprint Style Guide & Lessons Learned
     2	
     3	## Core Philosophy
     4	The blueprint is a **bridge between the mathematics and the Lean formalization**. A reader should be able to read a blueprint entry and immediately understand the corresponding Lean declaration. Conversely, someone reading the Lean code should find the blueprint proof sketch faithful to what the code actually does.
     5	
     6	## General Principles
     7	1. **Blueprint ↔ Lean must match.** Every `\lean{X}` tag must correspond to an actual Lean declaration. Every proof sketch must match what the Lean proof actually does — not a hand-wavy version of it.
     8	2. **Standalone.** `blueprint/` and any slides are independent — no cross-references, no shared files. Each has its own macros, its own `references.bib`.
     9	3. **Mathematical language only — zero Lean jargon.** No Lean identifiers in prose (no `selfImprovement_step`, no `PastingLemma.aux`, no `rintro ⟨X, hX⟩`). The `\lean{...}` tag is the link; the body text is standard mathematics. If you can't say it in math, rewrite it.
    10	4. **No filler prose.** Only precise definitions, theorem statements, and proof sketches. No "this is important because..." or "the self-improvement step governs the induction...".
    11	5. **Cite non-trivial things.** Basic definitions don't need citations. Important results and non-obvious definitions should cite the source paper.
    12	6. **Don't invent terminology or notation.** Don't create ad-hoc notation when standard notation exists. Don't name things that the literature doesn't name.
    13	7. **Match Lean's theorem/lemma/def exactly.** If Lean says `theorem X`, use `\begin{theorem}`. If Lean says `lemma X`, use `\begin{lemma}`. `\begin{proposition}` is allowed in blueprint prose when it improves mathematical readability, but still map it to an actual Lean `theorem`/`lemma` declaration via `\lean{...}`. Label prefix: `thm:` for theorem, `lem:` for lemma, `def:` for definition, `prop:` for proposition.
    14	
    15	### Remark On Mathematical Prose
    16	
    17	Blueprint entries should read as mathematical exposition, not as progress
    18	reports. The mathematical argument should determine the order of the prose:
    19	introduce the notation, state the assertion, give the proof or calculation, and
    20	then record Lean references through the usual blueprint tags. Lean declarations,
    21	file paths, and proof-status information should not become the visible structure
    22	of the paragraph. When referring to a source article, cite it bibliographically
    23	rather than relying on an uncited reference to the article.
    24	
    25	Use displayed formulae when the formula benefits from visual separation, and
    26	keep short scalar definitions or elementary inequalities inline when the
    27	sentence reads better that way. As in ordinary mathematical writing, displayed
    28	formulae should be punctuated as part of the sentences in which they occur.
    29	
    30	## Proof Sketches Must Match Lean
    31	This is the most important rule. Every proof in the blueprint must faithfully describe what the Lean proof does:
    32	
    33	- **Reference the actual lemmas used.** If the Lean proof calls `LDT.selfImprovement`, the blueprint proof should say "By Lemma X.Y (self-improvement)..." and list it in `\uses`.
    34	- **Do not use `\cref` or `\Cref`.** The blueprint does not load `cleveref`.
    35	  Spell out the kind of object and use ordinary references, for example
    36	  `Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement}` or `Theorem~\ref{thm:main-formal}`.
    37	- **Describe the actual proof structure.** If Lean does induction on a parameter, say so. If Lean uses a specific decomposition, name it.
    38	- **Don't hand-wave where Lean is specific.** "Standard argument" is not acceptable if Lean uses three specific lemmas. Name them.
    39	- **Don't be more specific than Lean.** If Lean uses `simp` to close a goal, a one-line sketch is fine.
    40	- **`\uses` in proofs must be accurate.** Only list what the proof actually uses, not what the statement mentions.
    41	
    42	## Source-Labelled Statements And Conditional Helpers
    43	
    44	If a blueprint theorem, lemma, or proposition carries a source label from the
    45	paper, the linked Lean declaration must state the same theorem, up to faithful
    46	formal encoding of the paper's domain.  Do not use `\lean{...}` and `\leanok`
    47	on the source-labelled statement to point to a conditional helper whose
    48	additional assumptions supply an unproved part of the paper proof.
    49	Changing the Lean statement away from `references/ldt-paper/` is strongly
    50	discouraged unless faithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical
    51	necessity requires it; the blueprint should make any such necessity explicit.
    52	
    53	Boundary hypotheses such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
    54	positivity of parameters, and denominator nonvanishing may be faithful when
    55	they express the mathematical domain that the paper leaves implicit.  By
    56	contrast, bridge inputs, residual data, repair hypotheses, producer
    57	assumptions, proof-obligation inputs, or package assumptions are proof debt.
    58	They must not be added to a source-labelled theorem statement.  If such data is
    59	still unproved, the source-labelled Lean theorem should keep the source-shaped
    60	statement and carry a tracked `sorry`, or the missing assertion should appear
    61	as the lowest named internal obligation with a tracked `sorry`.  A separately
    62	named conditional helper should not be introduced as a repair pattern.  If one
    63	already contains substantial proof content, it may remain temporarily only as
    64	quarantine: it needs a paper source, a tracking issue, and a discharge or
    65	deletion plan.  The blueprint should leave the paper theorem unmarked as
    66	proof-complete until the source-faithful Lean statement has a source-faithful
    67	proof.
    68	
    69	If a Lean theorem proves only a restricted version of a source theorem, the
    70	blueprint entry carrying `\leanok` must state that restriction in the theorem
    71	statement itself.  It must not be cited as the unrestricted source theorem.
    72	When the only Lean declaration available for a source label has extra
    73	non-paper assumptions, remove the `\leanok` claim from the source-labelled
    74	entry or move the restricted statement to a separate Lean-only entry.  The
    75	unrestricted paper theorem remains unformalized until a Lean statement with
    76	the source's hypothesis set exists.
    77	
    78	## Notation Consistency
    79	Notation must be **internally consistent** across the entire blueprint and **close to what the Lean code expresses**:
    80	
    81	- **Indices**: 0-indexed where matching `Fin n` in Lean
    82	- **Finite fields / alphabets**: use standard notation for the alphabet $\Sigma$ and finite fields $\mathbb{F}_q$
    83	- **Measurements**: use standard quantum measurement notation (projective measurements, POVMs)
    84	- **Strategies**: quantum strategies for nonlocal games should use standard notation from the literature
    85	- **Expansion**: use standard notation for graph expansion parameters
    86	- **Macros** (in `macros/common.tex`): define project-specific macros and use them consistently
    87	
    88	The original reference controls notation whenever it gives a usable convention.
    89	If the blueprint needs a different symbol, index convention, or name in order to
    90	match Lean, introduce it explicitly and relate it to the paper notation in the
    91	same paragraph.  Do not let a `\lean{...}` tag, a Lean namespace, or a file name
    92	be the only explanation of a changed term.
    93	
    94	When a public Lean declaration is a formalization-only auxiliary lemma, the
    95	blueprint should say so before listing the declaration.  The surrounding prose
    96	should identify the paper theorem, equation, or construction that the auxiliary
    97	lemma supports, and should avoid making the auxiliary name look like a named
    98	result from the source article.
    99	
   100	## What NOT to Put in the Blueprint
   101	- **Lean identifier names in math text.** Write "the self-improvement lemma", never "the `selfImprovement` step". The `\lean{LDT.selfImprovement}` tag handles the linking.
   102	- **Implementation details.** Don't say "bundled as an element of the Euclidean space" or "using `EuclideanSpace.equiv`". Describe the mathematical object.
   103	- **Ad-hoc notation.** Don't invent superscripts or subscripts to distinguish from existing notation. Use standard conventions.
   104	- **Function-call syntax.** Use mathematical notation, not programming notation.
   105	- **Redundant definitions.** If two blueprint definitions describe the same mathematical object, consolidate them. Each definition should introduce genuinely new mathematical content.
   106	- **Lean namespace prefixes in prose.** Don't write "the `LDT.PastingLemma`" — write "the pasting lemma".
   107	
   108	## Banned AI/Software Language (enforced in both blueprint AND Lean code)
   109	The blueprint reads as a **mathematical document**, not software documentation. The following patterns are banned in ALL reader-facing text (section titles, theorem names, proof sketches, remarks, chapter preambles) and in ALL Lean docstrings, comments, and section names:
   110	
   111	### Banned terms → replacements:
   112	| Banned | Use instead |
   113	|--------|------------|
   114	| "Assembly" (as section/chapter title) | "Proof of [theorem]", "Construction", "Composition" |
   115	| "Pipeline" | "reduction", "construction", "proof chain" |
   116	| "Bridge" (as noun for a connection) | "connection", name by mathematical content |
   117	| "Handoff" / "hand off" | "transition", "continuation", or drop entirely |
   118	| "In this blueprint" / "Within this blueprint" | "here", "in what follows", or omit |
   119	| "Honest" (as adjective for rigorous) | "exact", "faithful", "unconditional", "complete" |
   120	| "Glue layer" | "intermediate construction", "connecting results" |
   121	| "Re-export" / "reexport" | "provides", "re-states" |
   122	| "Wiring" / "wire up" | "connecting", "composing", "combining" |
   123	| "Package" (as noun for a data bundle) | "form", "data", "structure" |
   124	| "Sorry-free" | acceptable only in Lean-specific technical context |
   125	
   126	### Additional rules:
   127	- **Section names in Lean**: use mathematical terms (`section QuantumSoundness`, `section SelfImprovement`, `section PastingLemma`), not organizational terms (`section Assembly`, `section Pipeline`).
   128	- **Internal LaTeX labels** (e.g., `\label{ch:soundness}`) are not reader-facing and need not be renamed if doing so would break cross-references. But NEW labels should follow the standard.
   129	- **Definitions that are actually theorems**: if a statement asserts a mathematical fact, it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not `\begin{definition}`. Definitions introduce new objects; theorems prove properties.
   130	
   131	## `\uses` Dependency Guidelines
   132	- **Statement `\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.
   133	- **Proof `\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.
   134	- **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.
   135	
   136	## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
   137	Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
   138	from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
   139	look as if the paper stated them.
   140	
   141	- If a declaration directly formalizes a paper or blueprint statement, record
   142	  it as usual with `\lean{...}` on that statement and cite the relevant source.
   143	- If a public declaration is an auxiliary lemma introduced only for the Lean

Review this PR for TWO categories ONLY:
  (A) blueprint ↔ Lean **mathematical equivalence and status accuracy**;
  (B) prose quality — banned AI/software language AND no Lean jargon.

Authoritative source for category B: `docs/mathematical_language.md`. Read it once
before reviewing; do not paraphrase the tables here.

All other concerns (proof integrity, Mathlib style, performance, etc.)
belong to the code-review jobs of the `PR Review` workflow — do NOT comment
on them.

PR: <REPOSITORY>/pull/<PR_NUMBER>
Trigger: <EVENT>

Use `gh pr diff <PR_NUMBER>` to see the diff.

---

## Category A — 🟡 Blueprint ↔ Lean equivalence and status

This is the **core** check. The blueprint must not merely *link* to a Lean
declaration via `\lean{...}` — it must state the **same mathematical
content**, and its `\leanok` / `\notready` status tags must reflect
reality. `leanblueprint checkdecls` only verifies that tags resolve; YOU
verify they are *correct*.

For every `\lean{Namespace.Name}` tag in a `.tex` file changed in this PR,
and for every Lean declaration added or modified in this PR that has a
blueprint counterpart, do the following four checks:

### A.1 — Mathematical equivalence

Read the blueprint statement in `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` and the
corresponding Lean declaration in `MIPStarRE/...`. Compare them on every
axis that matters:

- **Quantifiers and hypotheses.** Does every blueprint hypothesis appear
  in the Lean signature, with the same strength? Watch for silent
  weakening ("primitive" in blueprint vs "irreducible" in Lean) or
  silent strengthening ("for all $A$" in blueprint vs implicit
  `[Nontrivial A]`/`[Fintype d]`/etc. in Lean that the blueprint
  omits).
  For a theorem, lemma, or proposition that cites a paper statement,
  an additional bridge, residual, repair, package, producer, witness, wrapper, proof-obligation input, or generic hypotheses bundle, generic assumptions bundle, or arbitrary
  hypothesis input is a mathematical mismatch. The only acceptable extra
  hypotheses are boundary conditions genuinely needed to state the same
  mathematics in Lean, such as positivity for a division, nonemptiness,
  decidability, or a field-model instance. Proof-debt objects are not
  boundary conditions.
  Missing proof work belongs as a tracked `sorry` on the source-faithful
  theorem, as a source-faithful lemma target to be proved from the same
  hypotheses, or as a paper-gap report; it must not become a bundled hypothesis
  consumed by downstream code.  Do not recommend adding a conditional helper
  merely to make a blueprint link pass.  An existing conditional helper may
  remain only as temporary quarantine for already useful proof content, with an
  explicit discharge or deletion plan, and it must stay off the paper theorem's
  `\leanok` path.
- **Conclusion.** Does the blueprint conclusion match the Lean return
  type? Watch for "$X$" vs "$X^\dagger$", "$=$" vs "$\leq$", strict
  vs non-strict inequalities, and conjugate-linear vs linear conventions
  (e.g. `mpvOverlap A B N = star (mpvInner A B N)` — the project's own
  `Fact-Check Lessons` in `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` calls this out).
- **Indexing conventions.** Blueprint indices run 0 to d−1 (matching
  `Fin d`). Flag if the blueprint silently uses 1 to d.
- **Definitions vs theorems.** If the blueprint asserts a fact ("X is a
  subalgebra"), it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not
  `\begin{definition}`.
- **Notation drift.** Does the blueprint use the established notation
  from `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` §"Notation Consistency"? Ad-hoc
  notation that disagrees with the Lean object is a sync bug.

For each mismatch, cite both the blueprint line and the Lean line, and
describe the mathematical discrepancy precisely. Do NOT accept "close
enough" — sync means equivalence, not similarity.

### A.2 — `\leanok` accuracy

`\leanok` on a `\begin{definition}`/`\begin{theorem}`/`\begin{lemma}`
asserts that the *statement* is formalized. `\leanok` inside
`\begin{proof}` asserts that the *proof* is fully formalized.

For every `\leanok` in changed .tex files (and for every newly proven
Lean theorem in the diff that should bear one):

- **Statement `\leanok`** is valid iff `\lean{Name}` resolves AND the
  Lean declaration's signature matches per A.1. If A.1 finds a
  mismatch, the `\leanok` is invalid.
- **Proof `\leanok`** is valid iff the corresponding Lean proof contains
  **no `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide` on non-trivial goals**, and no
  `axiom` introduced in this PR. Read the Lean proof body and check.
  `grep -n 'sorry\|admit' MIPStarRE/...` is a quick first pass.
- **Missing `\leanok`** is also a sync bug only when the Lean declaration
  is fully formalized, contains no proof-evasion device, and is
  source-faithful under A.1.  Do not recommend `\leanok` for a
  conditional helper that has extra non-paper hypotheses.
- **Open internal obligations** may be linked by `\lean{...}` for
  traceability only when the link clarifies a genuine proof frontier.  They
  must not be placed inside an existing `\leanok` block when they contain
  `sorry`, depend on `sorryAx`, or intentionally represent proof debt.  Do not
  ask authors to create or link conditional helpers merely to avoid a `sorry`;
  the preferred source-realignment repair is the source statement with a
  tracked `sorry`, or the lowest named internal obligation with a tracked
  `sorry`.  If a renamed declaration is still an open obligation, prefer a
  separate remark or implementation note with `\lean{...}` and no `\leanok`.

### A.3 — `\notready` accuracy

`\notready` means "the blueprint entry itself is not yet ready for
formalization" (e.g. statement still being clarified). Flag any
`\notready` on an entry whose Lean counterpart already exists and
matches — the blueprint clearly *is* ready and the tag is stale.

### A.4 — Tag presence and `\uses{...}`

- **New Lean declaration with no blueprint entry**: must add a
  `\begin{definition/theorem/lemma}` block with `\lean{...}`,
  appropriate status tag, and `\uses{...}` for dependencies.
- **Newly closed `sorry`** in Lean: blueprint `\begin{proof}` for that
  theorem must gain `\leanok`.
- **Removed or renamed Lean declaration**: blueprint must drop or
  rename the corresponding `\lean{...}` tag; otherwise
  `leanblueprint checkdecls` will fail.
  If the renamed declaration is an open internal obligation with `sorry`, do
  not demand that it be added to a source-labelled theorem block carrying
  `\leanok`; require only a non-`\leanok` traceability entry when the
  declaration is mathematically useful to mention.
- **`\uses{...}` accuracy**: a proof's `\uses` must match the lemmas the
  Lean proof actually invokes. Do not list everything the statement
  mentions; do not omit lemmas the proof uses.

## Category B — 🟡 Prose quality and no-Lean-jargon

**Read `docs/mathematical_language.md` before reviewing.** It is the single
authoritative source for:
  §1 — no Lean jargon in blueprint prose;
  §2 — banned software-engineering terms;
  §3 — banned LLM writing patterns.

Scope: blueprint `.tex` and Lean docstrings/comments/`section`

`references/ldt-paper/`.

For each finding, cite the exact phrase, link to the line, and propose
a concrete replacement from the table (or "drop").

    32	    (D : DirectLdParams) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin D.m) (DirectScalarQ D))
    33	    (hp : ∀ i, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p ≤ D.d) (i : Fin D.m) :

    40	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    41	    {g h : MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial params} (hpoly : g.poly = h.poly) : g = h := by
    42	  cases g with
    43	  | mk gp hg =>
    44	      cases h with
    45	      | mk hp hh =>
    46	          simp only at hpoly
    47	          subst hp
    48	          rfl

    50	/-- Bounded QPBT polynomial representatives are equivalent to mature LDT
    51	polynomial outcomes.  The variable renaming is the same coordinate reversal
    52	as `directPointEquiv`, so evaluation retains the direct coordinate order. -/
    53	noncomputable def directPolyEquivPolynomial (D : DirectLdParams) :
    54	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    55	    PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d ≃
    56	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
    57	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    58	  refine
    59	    { toFun := fun g =>
    60	        { poly := MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1
    61	          lowIndividualDegree := directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.1
    62	            (degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc g.2) }
    63	      invFun := fun g =>
    64	        ⟨MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.poly, ?_⟩
    65	      left_inv := ?_
    66	      right_inv := ?_ }
    67	  · rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree]
    68	    intro s hs i
    69	    exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp
    70	      (directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.poly g.lowIndividualDegree i)) s hs
    71	  · intro g
    72	    apply Subtype.ext
    73	    change MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev
    74	      (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1) = g.1
    75	    rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    76	    rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]
    77	    exact MvPolynomial.rename_id_apply g.1
    78	  · intro g
    79	    cases g with
    80	    | mk p hp =>
    81	        have hpoly : MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev
    82	            (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev p) = p := by
    83	          rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    84	          rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]
    85	          exact MvPolynomial.rename_id_apply p
    86	        apply ldtPolynomial_ext
    87	        exact hpoly

   119	/-- Regard a complete mature LDT measurement as a matrix-valued QPBT
   120	measurement, with exactly the same effects. -/
   121	noncomputable def ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement
   122	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   123	    (M : MIPStarRE.LDT.Measurement alpha iota) :
   124	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=
   125	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne M.outcome M.outcome_pos (by
   126	    rw [M.sum_eq_total, M.total_eq_one])

   128	@[simp] theorem ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement_effect
   129	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   130	    (M : MIPStarRE.LDT.Measurement alpha iota) (a : alpha) :
   320	The diagonal-block conditional expectation preserves either mixed defect
   321	exactly because the point measurement on the opposite carrier is constant on
   322	the residue register.  It does not yield a global/global compression theorem:
   323	the lifted state pairs equal residues, whereas separately compressing both
   324	polynomial measurements produces an independent double average over residues.
   325	Neither quantity bounds the other in general.  This open obstruction is
   326	recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
   327	-/
   328	
   329	/-- The normalized diagonal-block average of an operator on a carrier with a
   330	finite ancillary register.  This is the local conditional expectation used to
   331	discard one half of the correlated seed-residue ancilla. -/
   332	noncomputable def averageDiagonalBlock
   333	    {iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   334	    (A : Op (iota × block)) : Op iota := by
   335	  classical
   336	  exact (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   337	    ∑ r, A.submatrix (fun i => (i, r)) (fun i => (i, r))
   338	
   339	/-- Compress a POVM through the normalized diagonal-block average.  The
   340	nonemptiness assumption says precisely that the normalized finite average is
   341	defined over at least one ancillary basis element. -/
   342	noncomputable def correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement
   343	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   344	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   345	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   346	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) :
   347	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=
   348	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   349	    (fun a => averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a))
   350	    (fun a => by
   351	      unfold averageDiagonalBlock
   352	      apply smul_nonneg
   353	      · positivity
   354	      · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun r _ =>
   355	          Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   356	            ((Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (M.pos a)).submatrix
   357	              (fun i => (i, r))))
   358	    (by
   359	      classical
   360	      ext i j
   361	      simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply,
   362	        Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   363	      calc
   364	        ∑ a, (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   365	              ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) =
   366	            (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   367	              ∑ a, ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   368	                rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   369	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   370	              ∑ r, ∑ a, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   371	                rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   372	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   373	              ∑ r, (1 : Op (iota × block)) (i, r) (j, r) := by
   374	                congr 1
   375	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   376	                intro r _
   377	                simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
   378	                  congrFun (congrFun M.sum_eq_one (i, r)) (j, r)
   379	        _ = (1 : Op iota) i j := by
   380	              simp [Matrix.one_apply, Fintype.card_ne_zero])

   382	@[simp] theorem correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_effect
   383	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   384	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]

   386	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) (a : alpha) :
   387	    (correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement M).effect a =
   388	      averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a) :=

   392	    {alpha iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]

   396	  classical

    27	/-! ## Equality of the two consistency formulations -/
    28	
    29	-- The pure-state/Euclidean-vector bridge and the associated quadratic-form
    30	-- conversion are shared with the distance calculus, where they are stated for
    31	-- an arbitrary finite index type; see
    32	-- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistanceTheorems/Support.lean`.  The aliases below keep
    33	-- the names under which the transport statements in this file, and their
    34	-- downstream consumers, refer to that shared API.
    35	export MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus (pureStateEuclideanVector
    36	  pureStateEuclideanVector_apply pureStateEuclideanVector_norm
    37	  pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev)
    38	
    39	/-- For complete projective families and a pure bipartite state, the mature
    40	LDT consistency relation is exactly the QPBT off-diagonal defect.  In
    41	particular, changing between the density and vector formulations incurs no
    42	loss in the error parameter. -/
    43	theorem consRel_iff_consistencyDefect
    44	    {Question Outcome iotaA iotaB : Type*}
    45	    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
    46	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    47	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
    48	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
    49	    [Nonempty (iotaA × iotaB)]
    50	    (psi : PureState (iotaA × iotaB))
    51	    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    52	    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaA)
    53	    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaB) (delta : ℝ) :
    54	    ConsRel (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    55	        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta ↔
    56	      consistencyDefect mu
    57	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    58	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    59	        (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) ≤ delta := by
    60	  let AM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    61	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.leftPlacedMeasurement
    62	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (A x).toMeasurement)
    63	  let BM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    64	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.rightPlacedMeasurement
    65	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement)
    66	  have hAM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
    67	      (AM x).effect a = heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1 := rfl
    68	  have hBM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
    69	      (BM x).effect a = heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a) := rfl
    70	  have hdefect :
    71	      consistencyDefect mu
    72	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    73	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    74	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
    75	        bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    76	          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
    77	    calc
    78	      consistencyDefect mu
    79	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    80	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    81	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
    82	          1 - avgOver mu (fun x => ∑ a,
    83	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
    84	              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
    85	            simpa only [hAM, hBM] using
    86	              DistanceCalculus.consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
    87	                mu AM BM (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) hmu
    88	                  (pureStateEuclideanVector_norm psi)
    89	      _ = avgOver mu (fun x => 1 - ∑ a,
    90	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)

     6	/-!
     7	# The directly indexed low-degree game
     8	
     9	The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
    10	dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
    11	coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
    12	requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
    13	directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.
    14	
    15	The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
    16	uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
    17	determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
    18	formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.
    19	
    20	The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
    21	the mature low individual degree test interface: `Transport.Correspondence`
    22	identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
    23	presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
    24	direct strategy by a correlated residue register; `Transport.Questions` reads
    25	mature lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers; and
    26	`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as a
    27	mature `ProjStrat`, with exact Born-weight formulas for both adapters; and
    28	`Transport.Consistency` identifies polynomial outcomes and transports the
    29	three mature consistency conclusions to the direct game.
    30	
    31	## References
    32	
    33	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    36	The need for the directly indexed repair in Chapter 15 is explained around
    37	`rem:qld-4-7-divisibility` in
    38	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293` and in
    39	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    40	-/

   match t, a with

     (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
     (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=

     LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=

 \chapter{The Pauli basis test}
 \label{chap:qpbt-test}
 % Paper label sec:pauli-verifier kept for cross-reference fidelity; it resolves to this chapter.
 \label{sec:pauli-verifier}
 
 This chapter defines the two testing primitives underlying the question-reduction step: the \emph{classical low individual degree game}, in its simultaneous form, and the \emph{Pauli basis test}, a nonlocal game built from the classical game together with the Magic Square game. We state the quantum soundness of the classical game (Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}, imported, with the facts required by the identification, which remain to be proved, recorded in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; see Remark~\ref{rem:ld-soundness-provider}), the rigidity of the Magic Square game (Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity}, imported), completeness of the Pauli basis test (Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}), and the main soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test (Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}), whose proof occupies Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}--\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} and is completed in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} only modulo the proof obligation documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}. The chapter closes with the qubit form of the soundness statement (Corollary~\ref{cor:pauli-binary}) and the canonical parameter choice with its soundness bound (Definition~\ref{def:introparams}, Lemma~\ref{lem:delta-bound}).
 
 Throughout, the two players are denoted $\mathrm A$ and $\mathrm B$; for $w \in \{\mathrm A,\mathrm B\}$ we write $\overline w$ for the other player. Games, strategies, values, conditionally linear (CL) functions and distributions, typed distributions sampled from the edges of a graph, and the state-dependent approximation $\approx_\delta$ between families of measurement operators are as in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-games}; the algebraic material on lines, canonical linear maps, the low-degree encoding, and generalized Pauli observables is from Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}.
 
 \section{The classical low individual degree game}
 % Paper labels sec:ld-verifier and sec:ld-game kept for cross-reference fidelity.
 \label{sec:ld-verifier}
 \label{sec:ld-game}
 
 The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.
 
 \begin{definition}[The classical low individual degree game: parameters and registers]\label{def:ld-game}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldGame}
 	\uses{def:game, def:admissible-size}
 	% The source fixes \N to be the set of positive integers
 	% (references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:6) and takes m, d, ldc in \N
 	% (references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:33-35),

 	% It is load-bearing: at d = 0 or k = 0 the prefactor a(dmk)^a of delta_ld in
 	% lem:ld-soundness vanishes, and at d = 0 the resulting exact conclusions fail
 	% (e.g. at (q,m,d,k) = (2,1,0,1) with eps = 1). The case k = 0, though it would
 	% hold trivially, is likewise outside the source's domain and is omitted.
 	The game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}$ is parametrized by a tuple $\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$, where $m, d, k \ge 1$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}), and $m$ divides $q$.  	\[
 		\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}} = \{\mathsf{Point}, \mathsf{ALine}, \mathsf{DLine}\}\;,
 	\]
 	and the distribution over type pairs $(t_{\mathrm A}, t_{\mathrm B})$ is uniform over $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}} \times \mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}}$. The ambient space is the direct sum $V = V_X \oplus V_I \oplus V_V$ of three register subspaces: the \emph{point register} $V_X \cong \F_q^m$, the \emph{coordinate register} $V_I \cong \F_q$, and the \emph{direction register} $V_V \cong \F_q^m$. Elements of $V$ are identified with triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q^m$. The question distribution and the win predicate of $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}$ are specified in Definitions~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} and~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} below.
 \end{definition}
 
 \begin{definition}[Question distribution of the classical low individual degree game]\label{def:ld-question-distribution}
 	\uses{def:ld-game, def:cl-func, def:cl-dist, lem:cl-concat, def:cl-canonical, def:line-representative}
 	Let $\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ be as in Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}. Define $L_{\mathsf{Point}}$ to be the $1$-level CL function on $V$ that projects onto $V_X$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
 	\begin{equation}
 		\label{eq:cl-ptf}
 		L_{\mathsf{Point}}(u,s,v) = (u,0,0)\;.
 	\end{equation}
 	For $s \in \F_q$, let $\chi(s)$ be the unique integer such that
 	\begin{equation}
 		\label{eq:chi-func}
 		s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m} + r
 	\end{equation}
 	for some $0 \le r < q/m$, where $s$ is interpreted as an integer in $\{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}$ under the identification of $\F_q$ with binary strings fixed in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}. Since $m$ divides $q$, when $s$ is uniformly distributed on $\F_q$ the index $\chi(s)$ is uniformly distributed on $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$. Define $L_{\mathsf{ALine}}$ by
 	\begin{equation}
 		\label{eq:cl-alnf}
 		L_{\mathsf{ALine}}(u,s,v) = \bigl(L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u),\, s,\, 0\bigr)\quad\text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V\;,
 	\end{equation}
 	where $i = \chi(s)$ and $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ denotes the canonical linear map with one-dimensional kernel spanned by $v$, used to compute canonical representatives of lines (Definition~\ref{def:line-representative}). Define $L_{\mathsf{DLine}}$ by
 	\begin{equation}
 		\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
 		L_{\mathsf{DLine}}(u,s,v) = \bigl(L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),\, s,\, \pi_{i-1}(v)\bigr)\;,
 	\end{equation}
 	where $i = \chi(s)$ and $\pi_{i-1}$ zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of its input. The function $L_{\mathsf{DLine}}$ is the concatenation of (i) the identity on $V_I$, (ii) for each $i$ the $1$-level CL function $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ on $V_V$, and (iii) for each pair $(s,v') \in V_I \oplus V_V$ the $1$-level CL function $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_{v'}$ on $V_X$; thus $L_{\mathsf{DLine}}$ is a $3$-level CL function.

 \begin{lemma}\label{lem:alnf}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform, MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_mem_line}

Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$, and $\ell$ is a line that goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
 \end{lemma}
 \begin{proof}
 	\uses{def:line-representative}
 	Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$, the index $i = \chi(s)$ is uniformly random in $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$, so $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\ell(u_0,e_i)$. Since $u_0 = L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u)$ is the canonical representative of the line through $u$ in direction $e_i$, we have $u \in \ell(u_0,e_i)$.
 \end{proof}

 \end{lemma}

   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}
   176	
   177	Now we state our main theorem using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:prelims} below.
   178	This the formal version of \Cref{thm:main-informal}.
   179	
   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ 
   182	   which passes the  $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
   183	  Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
   184	  Let
   185	  \begin{equation*}
   186	  \nu = 100000 k^2m^4 \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/40000} + (d/q)^{1/40000} + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\Big).
   187	  \end{equation*}
   188	Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.
   205	As~$k$ increases, $\nu$'s prefactor $k^2$ increases.
   206	On the other hand, as $k$ increases, the term $e^{- k/(2560000m^2)}$ which also occurs in $\nu$ \emph{decreases}.
   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.
   209	We believe that this parameter~$k$ is an artifact of our proof,
   210	and we hope that it will be removed in the future.

291	\section{Candidate repairs}
   292	
   293	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
   294	Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
   295	$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
   296	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   297	$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
   298	this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,
   299	for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed
   300	$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game
   301	(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing
   302	else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
   303	lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
   304	does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
   305	the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
   306	arbitrary dimension.
   307	
   308	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
   337	  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
   339	  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
   340	  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
   341	  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
   342	  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
   343	  branch value is the diagonal average
   344	  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
   345	  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
   346	  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
   347	  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
   348	  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
   349	  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
   350	  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
   351	  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
   352	  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
   353	  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
   354	  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
   355	  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
   356	  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
   357	  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
   358	  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
   359	  obligation.
   360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
   364	  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
   365	  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
   366	  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
   367	  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
   368	  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
   369	  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
   370	  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
   371	  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
   373	  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
   374	  the import.)
   375	\end{itemize}

485	\begin{proof}
   486		\uses{def:line}
   487		Fix $u' \in \ell(u,v)$, so $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$. Any
   488		$a \in \ell(u,v)$ has the form $a = u + sv = u' + (s - t)v$, so
   489		$\ell(u,v) \subseteq \ell(u',v)$. The symmetric argument gives the reverse
   490		inclusion.
   491	\end{proof}
   492	
   493	Thus, for a fixed direction, a line is an equivalence class of its points: the
   494	pair $(u,v)$ representing it can use any base point on the line. A canonical
   495	representation is obtained as follows.
   496	
   497	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]\label{def:line-representative}
   498		\uses{def:line, def:cl-canonical, prop:line-equiv}
   499		Let $\ell$ be a line in direction $v \neq 0$, and let
   500		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v : \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with
   501		the one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$
   502		(Definition~\ref{def:cl-canonical}). The \emph{canonical representative of
   503		$\ell$} is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   504		\[
   505			u_0 = L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v(u) \qquad \text{for all } u \in \ell\;.
   506		\]
   507		This is well defined: since the image and kernel of $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ are
   508		complementary, any $u \in \ell$ decomposes uniquely as $u = u_0 + tv$ with
   509		$u_0$ in the image, so $u_0 = u - tv \in \ell$ and
   510		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v(u_0) = u_0$; moreover any two points of $\ell$ differ by
   511		a multiple of $v$ and therefore have the same image under
   512		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$. A line $\ell = \ell(u,v)$ is henceforth canonically
   513		represented by the pair $(u_0, v)$. (For $v = 0$, where the singleton
   514		$\{u\}$ leaves no independent kernel basis, we take $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_0$ to
   515		be the identity---the canonical linear map with empty kernel basis---so
   516		that $u_0 = u$; the source leaves this case implicit.)
   517	\end{definition}

+/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of
+its question type. -/
+theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv
+    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
+    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
+    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
+    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
+    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
+    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
+        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
+    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
+      if a = b then 0 else
+        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
+          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)
+
+/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
+outcome families. -/
+theorem consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv
+    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
+    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
+    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
+    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
+    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
+    consistencyDefect mu
+        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
+      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  apply avgOver_congr
+  intro x
+  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>
+    if a = b then 0 else
+      (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
+        (((A x a) * (B x b)).mulVec psi))).re
+  calc
+    _ = ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Beta, term (e a) (e b) := by
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro a _
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro b _
+      unfold term
+      by_cases hab : a = b
+      · subst b
+        simp
+      · have heab : e a ≠ e b := fun h => hab (e.injective h)

+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

+    (fun u a => heteroKron
+      ((maturePolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).outcome a) 1)
+    (maturePointBPlaced D S hS r)
+    (fun u a => heteroKron 1
+      ((matureCoordinatePointMeasurementB D S hS r u).outcome a)) S.ψ
+    (by intro u a; rfl) (by intro u a; rfl)
+  rw [directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_eq D S hS r G, heq]
+  exact hmature
+
+/-- Relabeling both global polynomial measurements identifies their direct
+QPBT defect with the mature global/global defect. -/
+theorem directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∀ (GA : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA)
+      (GB : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB),
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+          (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
+          (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
+          S.ψ =
+        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+          (fun _ g => maturePolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
+          (fun _ g => maturePolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro GA GB
+  calc
+    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
+        (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
+        S.ψ =
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ g => maturePolynomialLeftPlaced D GA (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g))
+        (fun _ g => maturePolynomialRightPlaced D GB (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g))
+        S.ψ := by
+          apply consistencyDefect_congr
+          · intro _ g
+            unfold maturePolynomialLeftPlaced
+            rw [directPolynomialMeasurement_effect]
+          · intro _ g
+            unfold maturePolynomialRightPlaced
+            rw [directPolynomialMeasurement_effect]
+    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ g => maturePolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
+        (fun _ g => maturePolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ :=
+      consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (directPolyEquivPolynomial D)
+        (fun _ g => maturePolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
+        (fun _ g => maturePolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ
+
+/-- Convert the global/global conclusion of `LDT.Test.mainFormal` to the direct
+QPBT defect, with the identical numerical bound. -/
+theorem directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∀ (GA : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA)
+      (GB : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB)
+      (delta : ℝ),
+      ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S) (uniformDistribution Unit)
+          (constSubMeasFamily GA.toSubMeas)
+          (constSubMeasFamily GB.toSubMeas) delta →
+        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+          (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
+          (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
+          S.ψ ≤ delta := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro GA GB delta h
+  have hmature := strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le S
+    (uniformDistribution Unit) (uniformDistribution_isProbability Unit)
+    (fun _ => GA) (fun _ => GB) delta h
+  have heq := consistencyDefect_congr (uniformDistribution Unit)
+    (fun _ g => maturePolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
+    (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.outcome g) 1)
+    (fun _ g => maturePolynomialRightPlaced D GB g)
+    (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.outcome g)) S.ψ
+    (by intro _ g; rfl) (by intro _ g; rfl)
+  rw [directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq D S GA GB, heq]
+  exact hmature
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Transport.Strategy
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems.TensorSupport
